transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (AE), Priya Nair (SE), Jordan Lee (PM), Sam Patel (AE), Maya Gonzalez (AE), Chris Turner (Sales Ops), Leah Ortiz (AE)

Auto-summary: internal SE enablement. Focus on updated messaging for Dedicated vs Hosted, competitive positioning vs Anthropic/OpenAI, demo practice with common customer Qs (security, latency, cost). Worked through a 10-minute demo script, called out places to emphasize KV cache, batching, and fallback policies. Identified action items to update collateral and schedule follow-up practice.

Topics: messaging, demo script, competitive objections, security talking points, benchmarking slides, next practice sessions.

[00:00] Alex: alright folks, welcome, thanks for joining our enablement. i'm alex, i'll be running through the agenda briefly. priya is gonna lead the demo practice and jordan has the updated deck notes. we've got about an hour, try to keep side convos to chat.
[00:18] Priya: hi everyone, quick housekeeping: recording on, slide deck in the chat, and the competitor battlecard link. i'll do a run of the demo, then we'll stop at pre-specified cue points for objections and messaging practice.
[00:32] Sam: sounds good, excited to see the updated positioning vs anthropic and openai.
[00:40] Jordan: quick note — we've added a slide that summarizes cost/latency tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated. it's intentionally simple: hosted = fastest time to value, predictable for smaller scale; dedicated = predictable throughput, better unit economics at scale + data isolation. we should practice the one-liners.
[01:05] Maya: can we surface an example where dedicated actually beats competitor X on cost? reps always ask for numbers.
[01:15] Priya: yes, we have a sample bench slide — it's approximate but shows 30-40% lower per-token cost for steady throughput when using dedicated w/ batching + quantization. caveat: depends on model and q-profile.
[01:30] Alex: remember to couch any numbers as "example/customer dependent" and point them to the benchmark doc. don't promise exact savings.
[01:45] Jordan: ok demo time. i'll hand it to priya, she's gonna do a 10-minute demo of a chat flow, call out routing, and show failure fallback to a smaller variant.
[02:00] Priya: starting demo — launching the Redwood Console, top left you can see model catalog, i'll pick a gpt-like open model, note we support streaming responses and function calling. i'll run a sample customer chat: "Plan my product launch timeline".
[02:28] Priya: <typing sounds>... output's generating, notice latency about 250ms per token in this sim. the demo environment is on a dev cluster so it's a bit noisy.
[02:45] Chris: quick interruption — how do we explain KV cache behavior to customers who think it's magical? they ask why subsequent prompts are faster.
[02:55] Priya: good q. say "KV cache stores key-value state for a session, so repeat prefixes or long-running conversations can reuse previous key/value tensors — reduces compute per token and speeds up subsequent calls." sometimes transcription will say KV 'cash' so watch language.
[03:20] Sam: we should have a one-liner for routing/fallbacks. customers worry about availability.
[03:28] Priya: suggested one-liner: "Redwood routes requests by policy (latency/cost/region) and automatically falls back to compatible variants to keep your app online — that means graceful degradation without customer-visible failures."
[03:45] Maya: does that get into our SLA? if we say fallback, will customers worry we're not reliable?
[03:52] Alex: tie to SLOs: "we offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated customers and robust fallbacks for hosted tiers; we build redundancy into routing to maintain service levels." keep it high level.
[04:10] Jordan: demo pause — cue point 1: security question. who's taking it?
[04:15] Priya: i'll handle. customer asks: "what about data residency and encryption?"
[04:20] Priya (demo voice): "we support Private/VPC deployments, KMS integrations for key management, and customers can choose region-specific hosting — plus SOC2 and ISO controls for auditability."
[04:32] Leah: do we have a crisp line on on-prem vs private? customers mix the terms.
[04:38] Jordan: recommended phrasing: on-prem = fully customer-managed stack (air-gapped option), private = customer-managed VPC with Redwood control plane. quick clarity avoids confusion.
[04:55] Sam: competitor angle — when customers ask why not OpenAI directly, what's the one-liner?
[05:02] Alex: "OpenAI is a great model provider; Redwood focuses on serving — making inference predictable and economical across hardware and deployment modes, plus enterprise controls (VPC, audit logs, SSO) that many OpenAI customers build themselves."
[05:25] Maya: anthropic tends to tout safety and instruction following — how do we handle that?
[05:32] Priya: match on safety: "we support red-teaming, evals, and quality monitoring; we also recommend model and quantization profiles by workload to avoid regressions." then pivot to serving differentiators.
[05:50] Jordan: demo resume — i'm going to show a canary rollout in Console. notice the route config and automatic fallback policies.
[06:10] Priya: (demo) i trigger a canary of a new model version for 10% traffic, set latency SLO to 200ms, and we have an automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[06:35] Chris: reps ask about pricing signals — if we push a new model that's more expensive, how to talk to finance?
[06:42] Alex: talk about unit economics: "higher quality model may cost more per token but can reduce calls via better prompts, or be isolated to premium routes; Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quantization to lower cost while keeping quality." emphasize tradeoffs.
[06:58] Sam: let's do the objection roleplay. Maya, you be customer skeptical of dedicated.
[07:05] Maya (roleplay): "Dedicated sounds expensive, why should I commit?"
[07:10] Priya (reply): "Dedicated is best when you have steady throughput and need predictable latency and data isolation; it's priced for committed throughput and can be 30-40% cheaper per token for steady usage versus bursty hosted consumption."
[07:30] Maya: i'd press on trial — what do we offer for evaluating dedicated?
[07:35] Alex: pilot programs: reserved capacity trials with limited commit and monitoring; encourage using our benchmark harness to run your typical traffic. add a line: "we'll help you model costs".
[07:50] Jordan: note for deck: add pilot pricing bullet.
[08:00] Priya: moving to the scripted demo second half — we'll simulate a spike and show autoscaling/burst capacity behavior.
[08:20] Priya: triggering spike... response times degrade slightly, routing shifts to burst pools and smaller variants to maintain throughput. in the demo you can see traces in the console.
[08:45] Sam: good to mention observability — Rep question: do we surface per-token cost in the console?
[08:53] Priya: yep, token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model are in console; show billing and traces.
[09:10] Maya: competitive quick note — Hugging Face marketplace customers sometimes want bring-your-own-model, how do we position?
[09:18] Alex: "We support model onboarding including customer BYOM; Redwood's runtime optimizations (kernel selection, compilation) give predictable performance, and we offer private deployments for regulated workloads."
[09:35] Jordan: cue point for demo handoff — real customer question: "What's the path to certs and audit logs?"
[09:42] Priya: "we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, provide audit logs for private deployments, and maintain SOC2 guidance; for enterprise customers we also provide compliance packages."
[10:00] Chris: small nit — reps often ask if SSO is included or extra.
[10:06] Alex: SSO (SAML/SCIM) is included in enterprise tiers; document the support levels.
[10:15] Priya: okay, practice the opening pitch. everyone take turns. Alex, you start.
[10:20] Alex (pitch): "Redwood Inference helps you ship LLM features faster with predictable economics — from hosted API to Private deployments. We focus on making inference economical and reliable across models and hardware so you don't have to build the serving stack yourself."
[10:40] Maya (feedback): good, add the mention of observability and rollouts in the middle.
[10:50] Sam (pitch): "We give you a consistent runtime and model lifecycle tooling — versioning, canary, fallback, and cost controls — so you can scale without surprises."
[11:05] Priya: demo interruption — small glitch in the demo. the environment hit a transient error; this is realistic and we should show how we'd handle it in call: apologize, explain fallback, and offer to run a bench for them.
[11:20] Jordan: annotate the script: at error, say "we're seeing a transient environmental issue in this demo; in production we provide SLA-backed Dedicated tiers and fallbacks to avoid visible downtime."
[11:40] Alex: let's roleplay some tougher competitive questions. Sam, you're a procurement lead asking about contractual controls.
[11:48] Sam (roleplay): "Do you offer data deletion guarantees and contract language around residency?"
[11:54] Priya (reply): "Yes — for Private deployments we can include specific residency and retention terms; for hosted we provide controls and can discuss contractual language with legal. point to the compliance package and SOC2 docs."
[12:12] Maya: how about encryption in-transit and at-rest specifics?
[12:18] Jordan: standard: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, customer-managed keys via KMS for Private. add note to not overshare implementation detail in sales calls.
[12:34] Chris: reps ask about onboarding time — what's typical for Private?
[12:40] Alex: Private can vary (weeks to months) depending on environment and approvals; dedicate an SE-led onboarding plan. Hosted is minutes to hours for basic API access.
[12:58] Priya: demo resumes — we'll show optimize features: recommendations for batching/quantization.
[13:10] Priya: (demo) open Optimize tab, recommend a quantization profile for the model, show expected latency/cost delta. emphasize recommendation is workload-specific.
[13:30] Sam: suggestion: add a short script for the recommendation that reps can read: "If your workload is high throughput and tolerant to slight quality variance, we recommend quantized profiles + batching to reduce costs."
[13:45] Jordan: will add to cheat sheet.
[14:00] Maya: let's practice objection pushback — "we're concerned about hallucinations".
[14:07] Priya: answer: "we couple model selection with prompt engineering, evals, and monitoring; Redwood's quality monitoring allows alerts on regression tied to eval prompts; we also suggest reranking or grounding for high-stakes tasks."
[14:25] Alex: call out real customer example (anonymized) where reranking reduced hallucinations in knowledge-base QAs. keep it brief.
[14:40] Sam: time check — we're halfway through. want to run a second demo iteration with two volunteers.
[14:48] Maya: i'll volunteer to mock a security-obsessed CTO.
[14:52] Priya: ok demo run two — starting again, but this time highlight observability traces and audit logs.
[15:09] Priya: (demo) show trace view: token-level timing and route selection. note that transcription sometimes labels speaker as "Speaker 2" — be cognizant of accuracy in notes.
[15:30] Maya (roleplay): "How do we prove compliance during procurement?"
[15:36] Priya (reply): "we provide SOC2 report and audit logs, plus a compliance package that outlines encryption, data flows, and certifications. for deeper audits we can coordinate with our security team."
[15:55] Jordan: pause — add to enablement deck: line item: "point to security docs and offer contact with security team."
[16:05] Alex: now competitive slide drill. Jordan, you call out top 3 competitor obs and reps respond with rebuttal.
[16:12] Jordan: competitor 1: OpenAI — claim is "best models and managed infra"; rebuttal?
[16:20] Maya: "OpenAI provides models; Redwood provides serving and enterprise controls — you get model access plus predictable runtime and private deployment options."
[16:34] Jordan: competitor 2: Anthropic — claim "safer models"; rebuttal?
[16:40] Sam: "We partner with safe model usage through evals and monitoring; more importantly, our platform optimizes how models are served and reduces operational burden."
[16:55] Jordan: competitor 3: AWS Bedrock — claim "integrated cloud ecosystem"; rebuttal?
[17:02] Priya: "Redwood focuses on inference economics and developer experience; we provide transparent perf profiles and tools that simplify rollouts across environments."
[17:20] Alex: good. a couple of seller tips: 1) don't call out pricing numbers publicly, 2) point to repo for benchmarks, 3) always offer a pilot.
[17:35] Chris: small point — reps need to know how to request bench support from SEs. what's the process?
[17:40] Jordan: file a bench request in the SE queue with sample prompt set, traffic pattern, and target SLOs; SE will schedule a bench and share results. add link to the process doc in chat.
[17:55] Priya: demo final stretch — show rollback and canary telemetry side-by-side.
[18:10] Priya: manual rollback triggered in console, system shows rollback reason: quality regression threshold hit. emphasize this in talking points.
[18:30] Maya: practice closing line — after demo, what do reps say?
[18:35] Sam (closing): "If you'd like, we can run a short pilot with your traffic to measure latency and cost, and we'll provide a benchmarking report within two weeks."
[18:50] Leah: that's solid; add a commitment language template.
[19:00] Alex: wrap up role plays and collect feedback. any outstanding objections?
[19:05] Maya: one more — how do we position when a customer has a strict data retention policy?
[19:12] Priya: mention retention config and contractual terms for enterprise; point to Private deployments for strict controls.
[19:25] Jordan: add an FAQ slide with retention/SSO/on-prem timelines.
[19:40] Chris: action items — I'll consolidate and send to the enablement list.
[19:45] Alex: let's recap next steps.
[19:48] Priya: recap: update demo script (alex), create benchmark slide (priya), add security notes to deck (jordan), schedule two practice sessions (chris).
[20:05] Sam: can we time-box the practice runs? prefer two 30-min sessions next Tues/Wed.
[20:12] Chris: noted, i'll send poll.
[20:20] Alex: any final Qs?
[20:22] Maya: none. good session.
[20:25] Alex: thanks everyone. recording will be uploaded. action items in chat. end.

Notes on transcript quality: some transcription glitches (KV cash, Redwood Dedicatede) — corrected in notes but left raw in the transcript in a few places to reflect auto-transcription issues.
